s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive breast mass with skin ulceration and underlying cystic-solid lesion
salient_findings: Palpable breast lump with progressive growth
Firm, immobile mass with indistinct borders
Loss of normal breast architecture on ultrasound
key_facts: 51-year-old woman
2-cm palpable right-breast lump in 2019
Progressive growth of the lump
Skin ulceration with straw-colored exudate by June 2021
Local pain but no systemic symptoms
No chronic medical history
Asymmetrically enlarged right breast
15×15 cm firm, immobile mass with indistinct borders
Erythematous, swollen, and dehiscent overlying skin
No axillary or clavicular lymphadenopathy
Mild anemia (hemoglobin 83 g/L)
Slightly low albumin
Normal blood counts and liver function tests
Loss of normal architecture on breast ultrasound
Cystic-solid lesion with internal fluid levels and tortuous vessels on CT and MRI
Dilated ducts with broad papillary structures on core needle biopsy
ER 90%, PR 90%, HER2 negative, Ki-67 20% on immunohistochemistry

shortlist.label: Invasive ductal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Most common type of breast cancer, matches clinical presentation of a progressive breast mass with skin ulceration

shortlist.label: Inflammatory breast cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of a rapidly progressing breast mass with skin changes, including erythema and edema

shortlist.label: Papillary carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Core needle biopsy revealed dilated ducts with broad papillary structures, consistent with papillary carcinoma

shortlist.label: Encapsulated papillary carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Shares similar histological features with papillary carcinoma, and is a plausible diagnosis given the clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Intraductal papillary carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Is a type of papillary carcinoma that arises within the ducts of the breast, consistent with the biopsy findings

raw.rationale: The presence of skin ulceration, erythema, swelling, and dehiscence, along with the rapid progression of the tumor, are characteristic features of inflammatory breast cancer. The absence of systemic symptoms and the localized nature of the disease also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Invasive ductal carcinoma
rejected.why: While invasive ductal carcinoma is a common type of breast cancer, the presence of skin changes and the aggressive nature of the tumor are more suggestive of inflammatory breast cancer.

rejected.label: Papillary carcinoma
rejected.why: Papillary carcinoma is a type of breast cancer that typically presents as a solid mass, but the presence of skin ulceration and erythema is not typical of this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Encapsulated papillary carcinoma
rejected.why: Encapsulated papillary carcinoma is a rare type of breast cancer that is typically well-circumscribed and does not exhibit the aggressive features seen in this case.

rejected.label: Intraductal papillary carcinoma
rejected.why: Intraductal papillary carcinoma is a type of breast cancer that is typically confined to the ducts and does not exhibit the invasive features seen in this case.

rejected.label: Invasive ductal carcinoma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and imaging findings are more consistent with inflammatory breast cancer than invasive ductal carcinoma.
